newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BOYD'S FIRST SCOTLAND GOAL SETS UP VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOYD'S FIRST SCOTLAND GOAL SETS UP VICTORY.

text.p: Tom Boyd's first goal for Scotland helped take his country a step closer to next year's World Cup finals when they defeated Estonia 2-0 in a Group four qualifying match on Saturday.

The Celtic defender had waited 43 appearances before finding the net in a Scottish jersey and the victory now puts Craig Brown's team four points ahead of second placed Austria, who they play in Glasgow on Wednesday.

More importantly, the result helped to atone for the embarrassing goalless draw with the Estonians in Monaco last month which had put unexpected pressure on them for this match, played out in front of a sellout 18,000 crowd at Rugby Park, hosting its first international since 1909.
The result, partizan support and occasion all vindicated the decision of the Scottish Football Association to play in a provincial town rather than a major city.
Scotland took only 25 minutes to overcome the stubborn nine-man defence deployed by the Estonians.

Boyd pounced for his goal after a shot from Chelsea's Craig Burley had been blocked by Estonian goalkeeper Mart Poom - who has just joined English premier league club Derby for 500,000 pounds ($815,000) - to head in the rebound.
Estonia, who had Sergei Hohlov-Simson and Indrek Zelinski booked, went further behind in the 53rd minute.
This time Boyd was the creator, supplying a cross which was intended for Blackburn's Kevin Gallacher but which was turned into the Estonian net by the unfortunate defender Janek Meet.
The defeat leaves Estonia, whose next match is in Austria in a month's time, on four points from four matches.
